statement_en: Hamilton's rule has NO rule-out direction over a design and was deliberately given no browser_check row. This is not a missing-input problem: supplying r, b and c would not make it bind.
proof_status: The statement itself is sound and is a candidate law; being unevaluable over a design is not the same as being unproved.
not_checkable_because: The law classifies the DIRECTION of change in a social trait. A row with op gt on r*b > c would report violated whenever a trait is predicted to DECREASE, and a costly trait that kin selection disfavours is an ordinary organism, not an impossible one. In a surface where red means "violates a law" that is a false positive, so no block was declared. The rejected block is kept in the law's meta under browser_check_absent.block_considered_and_rejected.
why_no_input_would_help: No input makes this bind. Nothing, as a design-level rule-out. It would become checkable only against a design that explicitly CLAIMS a social trait is maintained by kin selection; then r*b <= c refutes that claim. That is a claim-level check and the registry has no place for one today - which is itself a gap worth recording. The inputs the producing record listed (relatedness (regression coefficient); benefit_to_recipient (fitness units); cost_to_actor (fitness units)) are the quantities the statement is ABOUT, not quantities whose absence is the problem: supplying them yields a law that still rules nothing out.
false_positive_if_forced: The law classifies the DIRECTION of change in a social trait. A row with op gt on r*b > c would report violated whenever a trait is predicted to DECREASE, and a costly trait that kin selection disfavours is an ordinary organism, not an impossible one. In a surface where red means "violates a law" that is a false positive, so no block was declared. The rejected block is kept in the law's meta under browser_check_absent.block_considered_and_rejected.
what_it_would_take: Nothing, as a design-level rule-out. It would become checkable only against a design that explicitly CLAIMS a social trait is maintained by kin selection; then r*b <= c refutes that claim. That is a claim-level check and the registry has no place for one today - which is itself a gap worth recording.
found_by: Emitted by the LeanBio discovery agent (round 2) as a requirements record whose own verdict read "not-checkable-in-principle (no rule-out direction)". Re-typed here: a statement no input can make bind is neither waiting for data nor wrong, and carrying it as a requirements record would have read as "supply these numbers and the law will work", which its own not_checkable_because denies. The producing agent had flagged this by shouting the caveat inside its missing_inputs strings; that workaround is what prompted the new type.

scope_note: Static mirror of lean/registry/open-questions/. An OPEN QUESTION is a question this project holds unsettled, with an arm per live position, each arm's evidence quoted from its primary source, and a belief `proportion` COMPUTED by pipeline/leanbio/belief.mjs rather than asserted. A proportion orders the arms; it is NOT a probability that an arm is true, and belief-params.json says plainly that its parameters are hand-set and not fitted. No arm of an open question is in any law set, and the guard in openq-lib.mjs refuses to accept a law that asserts one. A FAILED THEOREM is a statement this project tried and could not establish, kept with its reason so nobody reproposes it; `what_survives` says what is still true after the failure. READ `attempted`: a failed-theorem record with `attempted: false` was NEVER TRIED (the single Lean build lock was contended, or it was abandoned on cost, or withheld on purpose), so it is not a result about the statement at all and its `proof_status` says so; the counts report attempted and never-attempted separately for that reason. A NOT-CHECKABLE-IN-PRINCIPLE record is a fourth thing: sound, usually proved, but with no falsifiable direction over any design, so NO input would make it bind -- it carries no `missing_inputs`, because a list of them would read as a to-do and misstate the finding. Arms formalised in Lean are proved internally consistent and are NOT proved true of any organism.
